Reference / toml/value

toml/value#

Immutable TOML values; not a TOML document parser or printer.

Version: v1.0.0

Synopsis#

let settings = TomlTable(
    TomlMember("name", TomlString("Ada")),
    TomlMember("enabled", TomlBoolean(true)),
);
settings.value("name").accept(observer);

Description#

Immutable TOML values; not a TOML document parser or printer.

accept() invokes exactly one typed TomlVisitor callback. It does not descend automatically into arrays or tables; the observer controls traversal and its exceptions propagate. No JSON conversion, kind-switch/downcast, reflection, I/O or implicit printing. Scalar coordinates retain their exact runtime type. Temporal coordinates include year zero, nanoseconds, leap-second notation and unknown zero offsets. They do not implicitly convert to host instants. See docs/std/toml-values-guide.md for the distinction and parser contract.

TomlArray/TomlTable snapshot size() once and item(i) once in increasing index order at construction. The source is borrowed and never closed. values() or members() returns the retained immutable snapshot, so repeated observation never traverses the original sequence. Snapshots are shallow nominal values; arbitrary custom TomlValue implementations are not inspected or frozen.

Defaults: 10000 array items, 1024 table members; a second constructor argument replaces the bound. InvalidTomlLimit rejects negative bounds before source observation, InvalidTomlSize rejects negative size(), TomlLimitExceeded rejects size above the budget before item reads. Zero allows empty containers. Bounds constrain cardinality, not scalar length or total nested graph size.

TomlMember binds an exact Unicode name to a TomlValue. Empty names and literal dots are valid. Tables preserve insertion order; duplicate exact names fail with DuplicateTomlMember. No case folding or Unicode normalization. Dotted source syntax is a parser concern. value(name) throws MissingTomlMember for absence; membership(name) returns false. Neither container claims to be a sequence/map itself. Duplicate validation is O(n²), lookup O(n), bounded by the configured member count. No resources or destroy/close hooks are owned.

Run: okkama run -t std/toml/value.ok

object TomlInfinity#

object TomlInfinity does TomlValue

Okkama builtin floats are finite. TOML's explicit special values therefore remain distinct immutable TomlValue objects and never masquerade as a native Float. Infinity preserves its sign; NaN sign/payload are unspecified by TOML and canonicalized. accept() invokes one dedicated callback, without arithmetic or implicit conversion. Finite TomlFloat continues to preserve binary64 bits.

inf, or -inf when negative.

object TomlTable#

object TomlTable does TomlValue

A table reads like json (#140): text(name), int(name), float(name), boolean(name), get(name) for a nested table, tables(name) for an array of tables, texts(name), ints(name), floats(name) and booleans(name) for arrays, local_date(name), local_time(name), local_date_time(name) and date_time(name) for the TOML dates, and maybe(name) for a key that may be absent:

let config = ParsedToml(text).root();
config.get("server").int("port");
config.maybe("debug").boolean() else false;
for config.tables("replica") -> replica { replica.text("host"); }

A missing key is MissingTomlMember; a value of another kind is TomlKindMismatch, which names the key and both kinds. No value is converted: an integer is not a float, and inf and nan are not floats either.

object TomlLocalTime#

object TomlLocalTime does TomlValue

The second coordinate can be 60 to preserve leap-second notation. This is NOT a claim that the coordinates identify a real scheduled leap event. Nanoseconds are integral; parsing longer fractions must truncate, not round.

enum TomlKindMismatch#

enum TomlKindMismatch is Error = (member(name is string, expected is string, found is string))

A value of another kind than the read asked for: the key (with [index] for an array item), the kind asked for and the kind found, as TOML names them: string, integer, float, inf, nan, boolean, array, table, local date, local time, local date-time, offset date-time.
